raw.assessment: The incumbent combines a predictable conversational routine with printed preparation and optional messaging. Seven frequent attendees explicitly value its repetition, and print serves nine regular print-only users. Familiarity may reduce entry effort for regulars, but that causal account is untested. H3-O6 supplies a concrete limit: five occasional attendees struggled to enter conversations familiar to partners. Pair delays and switches are consistent with entry friction but do not establish its cause. Useful-practice reports were 49/72 and correct preparation identification 48/72; neither establishes the targets across all 97 attendances. Coordination sometimes exceeded 90 minutes. Untimed practice, blanks, and unlinked slips limit attribution.

openings.claim: Unequal familiarity with conversational context may impede entry independently of proficiency.
openings.delta: Retain the repeated routine but test a self-contained first prompt supplying both partners the same starting context, without public proficiency labels or prior-attendance requirements.
openings.prediction: Relative to existing prompts, shared-context prompts reduce time to both partners' first substantive contribution and early partner switching, especially where prior familiarity differs.
openings.probe: Across six sessions, alternate comparable existing and shared-context prompts between pair groups. Observe entry latency, switches, and individual speaking duration; collect anonymous useful-practice reports and optional private familiarity responses. Keep practice inside 75 minutes and record added volunteer effort.
assumptions: Comparable prompts can be prepared within the coordination budget.
Observation can distinguish context-entry friction from unequal speaking turns; neither cause is established.

openings.claim: Preparation errors may partly reflect ambiguity about which week a task belongs to.
openings.delta: Test a paper calendar of six dated preparation tasks, reissued at attendance, with the next date visibly marked and each task usable after missed sessions.
openings.prediction: Earlier-task substitutions decrease; unchanged errors despite correct date recognition would weaken temporal ambiguity as the explanation.
openings.probe: Ask anonymous exit respondents separately for the next session date and preparation task. Compare error types with baseline, retain blanks in the denominator, record print-only responses, and log weekly coordination minutes including calendar preparation.
assumptions: Volunteers can select six conversational topics in advance within the weekly time target.
Advance paper copies remain usable during absences; attendance never depends on preparation.

raw.assessment: Supplied slips document 49/72 reports of ten useful speaking minutes and 48/72 correct preparation tasks; these do not establish rates across all attendees. Coordination sometimes exceeds 90 minutes. Entry friction and task-version confusion are plausible contributors, not demonstrated causes.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: a repeatable fresh-start pairing routine with balanced speaking turns could improve useful practice for occasional and frequent attendees.
openings.delta: Keep the familiar session structure but begin each pair with a self-contained prompt. Offer optional sentence supports and extension prompts without proficiency labels. Use alternating timed turns and a scheduled opportunity to change partners; handle odd attendance with a trio whose turns are equally allocated.
openings.prediction: Pair formation consumes fewer minutes and fewer occasional attendees report difficulty entering; useful-practice reports improve if entry and turn allocation are relevant causes. More timed speaking without improved usefulness would weaken that explanation.
openings.probe: Across six sessions, anonymously observe formation time and sampled speaking turns, and collect exit reports of useful minutes and optional recent attendance frequency. Record response coverage, including blanks, and total weekly coordination. Check the 80% useful-practice and under-90-minute targets rather than treating timed turns alone as success.
assumptions: Reusable prompts and brief volunteer timing fit within 75 minutes and unpaid coordination capacity.
Participants can choose support or extension material without publicly labeling proficiency.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: a single dated paper preparation instruction could reduce confusion between current and earlier tasks with little recurring coordination.
openings.delta: Put the next session date and one concrete preparation task in the same prominent location on every sheet, with a matching printed master at Wednesday sessions. Reuse the template; include an immediate conversational entry option for anyone arriving unprepared or after an absence.
openings.prediction: Earlier-task answers decline from the observed 12/72 and correct task identification reaches 85% of attendees, including printed-only users, without increasing coordination beyond the weekly limit.
openings.probe: At departure, ask anonymously for the next date and task and whether preparation information was obtained on paper. Track correct, stale, blank and missing responses against attendance. Log printing and clarification minutes separately across six sessions; check whether easier identification actually reduces coordination.
assumptions: Volunteers can select the next task before distributing sheets.
Wednesday paper access remains available to everyone; preparation is never required for participation.
Stale instructions contribute to errors; recall or comprehension may instead dominate.

openings.claim: Unequal context familiarity may impede entry independently of proficiency.
openings.discriminator: Shared-context prompts reduce entry latency and switching.
openings.probe: Alternate comparable prompts between groups; observe entry, switches, individual duration; privately ask optional familiarity.
openings.uncertainty: Entry friction versus unequal turns remains unresolved.

openings.claim: Fresh starts plus balanced turns may improve useful practice.
openings.discriminator: Timed speech without usefulness improvement weakens explanation.
openings.fit: Preserves routine; optional supports/extensions avoid labels.
openings.probe: Test self-contained prompts, alternating timed turns, scheduled partner changes and equal-turn trios; observe formation, turns, optional attendance frequency.
openings.uncertainty: Bundled causes and volunteer timing cost remain uncertain.

openings.claim: Temporal ambiguity may cause stale preparation answers.
openings.discriminator: Errors despite correct dates weaken explanation.
openings.fit: Six dated paper tasks; reissue with next date marked; tasks independent of attendance.
openings.probe: Ask date and task separately; log print-only results and calendar preparation cost.
openings.uncertainty: Advance topic selection and paper usability during absence untested.

openings.claim: One dated instruction may reduce confusion and recurring work.
openings.discriminator: Fewer stale answers and clarification minutes.
openings.fit: Reusable next-task sheet, matching printed master, immediate unprepared entry.
openings.probe: Count correct, stale, blank and missing answers; log printing and clarification separately.
openings.uncertainty: Recall/comprehension may dominate; next task must be ready.

post_distill.decision: Test distinct alternatives over six sessions; no established cause. Preserve free entry despite absence, nonpreparation or declined public labels; offline access; conversational purpose; 75-minute room limit and unpaid facilitation. Check >=80% useful-practice reports, >=85% correct tasks and <90 weekly coordination minutes including setup. Use attendance denominators with blanks/missing visible; untimed, unlinked baseline slips cannot establish attendee-wide success.
